name: E-Commerce Defective Smartphone Refund Denial
raw_input: I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on an e-commerce app on 10th November 2024. It was delivered on 14th November. Within 24 hours of opening the box, the screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working. I raised a replacement request on 15th November. The app sent a technician for inspection on 21st November. The technician confirmed it is a manufacturing hardware defect and took sign on his job sheet. But on 23rd November, customer support cancelled my return request stating 'The 7-day return window expired on 21st November'. They are telling me to go to an authorized brand service center 40 km away. I paid for a brand new working phone, not a defective phone repaired on day one. I have the invoice, delivery receipt, technician inspection job sheet copy, and chat screenshots.

case_dossier.case_title: Defective Samsung Galaxy phone - Return denied
case_dossier.summary: The consumer purchased a Samsung Galaxy smartphone for Rs 26,999 on an e‑commerce app. The phone developed a hardware defect within a day, but the platform cancelled the return request citing an expired return window, directing the consumer to a distant service centre.

timeline.event: Placed order for Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on the e‑commerce app.
Within 24 hours of opening, screen flickered and touch stopped; consumer raised a replacement/return request.
Technician visited, inspected the phone, confirmed manufacturing hardware defect, and signed the job sheet.
Customer support cancelled the return request, stating the 7‑day return window expired on 21 Nov, and advised going to an authorized service centre 40 km away.

evidence_held: Invoice showing purchase price of Rs 26,999
Delivery receipt confirming receipt on 14 Nov 2024
Technician inspection job sheet (signed) indicating hardware defect
Chat screenshots with e‑commerce customer support regarding the return request and cancellation
evidence_needed: Video or photos clearly showing the screen flickering and touch failure
Original, unaltered copy of the technician’s report (if any additional notes beyond the job sheet)
Email or in‑app notification confirming the replacement/return request submission date
Written communication from the platform stating the 7‑day return policy terms
Proof of any additional costs incurred (e.g., travel to service centre) if seeking compensation
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Key documents (invoice, delivery receipt, signed technician sheet, chat logs) directly support the claim, giving the evidence a strong but not perfect rating.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You are a consumer as defined under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 because you bought a Samsung Galaxy phone for personal use. The phone turned out to be defective within a day, and a qualified technician has already confirmed a manufacturing fault. Under the Act, a defect in a product is a clear "deficiency in service" and the seller (including the e‑commerce platform that facilitated the sale) is required to either replace the product, repair it, or refund you. The platform’s refusal to honour a return, despite the defect being proven, amounts to an unfair trade practice. This is a civil matter – it is about getting your money back or a replacement, not about criminal cheating. You therefore have a strong legal right to seek a refund or replacement through the consumer dispute redressal system.

governing_laws.relevance: Defines you as a consumer, giving you standing to approach the consumer forum.
Classifies the hardware fault as a "deficiency in service" for which the seller is liable.
The platform’s refusal to accept a return despite a proven defect is an unfair trade practice.
Makes the manufacturer/seller liable to compensate you for harm caused by a defective product.
Gives you the right to file a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Clarifies that failure to refund or replace a defective product is a civil dispute, not a criminal offence.

action_options.title: Send a Formal Legal Notice to the Platform
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (postage or email cost)
action_options.details: Draft a concise notice stating: (a) you bought the phone on 10 Nov 2024, (b) it was defective on 15 Nov 2024, (c) a technician confirmed the defect, (d) the platform’s refusal violates Sections 2(11) & 2(47) of CPA 2019, and (e) you demand a full refund of Rs 26,999 or a replacement within 7 days. Send it by registered post or email and keep a copy of the receipt.

action_options.title: File a Consumer Complaint on the e‑Daakhil Portal
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fee for claims up to Rs 5 Lakhs
action_options.details: Register at edaakhil.nic.in, choose ‘Consumer Complaint’, and upload: invoice, delivery receipt, technician’s signed job sheet, chat screenshots, and a copy of the legal notice. Fill in the details of the dispute and request a refund. The portal guides you step‑by‑step and you can represent yourself.

action_options.title: Approach the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
action_options.timeline: Within 60‑90 days if the platform does not comply with the e‑Daakhil order
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal filing fee (around Rs 100‑200) plus any required stamp duty
action_options.details: If the e‑Daakhil process does not yield a satisfactory order, file a petition directly with the District Consumer Commission of the district where you reside. Attach all documents already uploaded on e‑Daakhil. You may appear personally; a lawyer is optional but not mandatory.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: Consumer forums allow self‑representation, so you can handle the notice and the e‑Daakhil filing yourself. You would only need a lawyer if the platform files an appeal in a higher consumer commission or if you want professional help preparing evidence for a court‑level case.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**[Your Name]**  
[Your Complete Residential Address]  
[City, State – PIN]  
Mobile: [Your Mobile No.] | Email: [Your Email‑ID]  

---

### LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE  
*(Under instructions from my client – the consumer)*  

---

**Date:** 7 November 2026  

**Mode of Dispatch:** Speed Post (Acknowledgement Due) / Registered Email (with read‑receipt)  

**To,**  

The Manager – Legal/Customer‑Care  
[Name of the E‑Commerce Platform]  
[Corporate Office Address]  
[City, State – PIN]  

---

#### 1.  SUBJECT  
**Demand for Refund/Replacement of Defective Samsung Galaxy Smartphone (Order No. __________) – Failure to Honour Return Request in Violation of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.**  

---

#### 2.  FACTUAL MATRIX  

| Sr. No. | Date / Period | Event |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| 1 | **10 Nov 2024** | Placed an order for a **Samsung Galaxy smartphone** (Model – __________) on your e‑commerce app, paying **Rs 26,999** (Invoice No. __________). |
| 2 | **14 Nov 2024** | The product was delivered at my residence (Delivery Receipt No. __________). |
| 3 | **15 Nov 2024** (within 24 hrs of unboxing) | Screen began flickering; touch‑panel stopped responding. Immediately raised a **replacement/return request** through the app (in‑app notification dated 15 Nov 2024). |
| 4 | **21 Nov 2024** | A certified technician from an authorized service centre inspected the device, **confirmed a manufacturing hardware defect**, and signed the job‑sheet (Annex‑C). |
| 5 | **23 Nov 2024** | Your customer‑support team **cancelled** the return request, stating that the 7‑day return window had expired on 21 Nov 2024, and directed me to an authorized service centre **40 km away** (Chat screenshots – Annex‑D). |

All the above documents (invoice, delivery receipt, technician’s job‑sheet, chat logs) are attached hereto as annexures.

---

#### 3.  LEGAL BASIS  

1. **Consumer Protection Act, 2019** –  
   * **Section 2(7)** defines me as a “consumer”.  
   * **Section 2(11)** treats the hardware fault as a “deficiency in service”.  
   * **Section 2(47)** classifies the refusal to accept a return of a defective product as an **unfair trade practice**.  
   * **Section 84** makes the seller liable to compensate the consumer for loss caused by a defective product.  

2. Under **[unverified reference removed]** of the Act, a consumer is entitled to **interest at the rate of 12 % per annum** on the amount due, from the date of default till actual payment.  

3. The refusal to honour a return despite a **certified defect** is a direct contravention of the above provisions and also violates the **e‑commerce platform’s own 7‑day return policy** (as communicated in the chat).  

---

#### 4.  DEMAND  

In view of the foregoing facts and legal provisions, I **hereby demand** that you, within **fifteen (15) days** from the receipt of this notice (i.e., on or before **22 November 2026**), do **either** of the following, at my option:  

1. **Refund** the full purchase price of **Rs 26,999** (Rupees Twenty‑Six Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety‑Nine only), **plus** statutory interest at **12 % per annum** calculated from **23 Nov 2024** till the date of actual payment, **and** reimbursement of any incidental expenses incurred (e.g., travel to the service centre).  

**OR**  

2. **Replace** the defective Samsung Galaxy smartphone with a brand‑new, identical model, free of any charge, and deliver it to my address within **seven (7) days** of your compliance with this notice.  

Kindly acknowledge receipt of this notice and intimate your intention to comply, within the stipulated period, by sending a written confirmation to the address/email mentioned above.  

---

#### 5.  CONSEQUENCES OF NON‑COMPLIANCE  

If you fail to comply with the above demand within the stipulated **15‑day** period, I shall be constrained to initiate **legal proceedings** without any further notice, which shall include but not be limited to:  

* Filing a complaint before the **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission** under **Section 35** of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019;  
* Claiming **interest at 12 % per annum**, **court costs**, **legal expenses**, and **punitive damages** as may be awarded by the forum; and  
* Seeking an order for **specific performance** (i.e., replacement of the product) or **full restitution** with interest.  

Such proceedings shall be instituted at my own cost and risk, and the platform shall be liable for **all consequential losses** arising therefrom.  

---

#### 6.  ANNEXURES  

| Annex‑No. | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Annex‑A** | Original Invoice showing purchase price of **Rs 26,999** |
| **Annex‑B** | Delivery receipt confirming receipt on **14 Nov 2024** |
| **Annex‑C** | Technician’s inspection job‑sheet (signed) confirming hardware defect |
| **Annex‑D** | Screenshots of chat with customer‑support showing cancellation of return request |
| **Annex‑E** | Copy of this Legal Demand Notice (for your records) |
| **Annex‑F** *(if any)* | Any additional evidence (photos/video of defect, travel receipts, etc.) |

---

#### 7.  DECLARATION  

I, **[Your Full Name]**, the undersigned, do hereby declare that the contents of this notice are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief, and that I am authorized to issue this notice on my own behalf.  

---  

**Signature of the Consumer**  

_____________________________  
[Your Full Name]  

**Date:** 7 November 2026  

---  

*Please retain a copy of this notice and the acknowledgement receipt for future reference.*

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under Section 2(11) and Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, delivering a defective phone and delaying inspection past your return window is a clear deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. I have the technician report confirming hardware fault. I demand an immediate refund or I will escalate to the National Consumer Helpline and e-Daakhil.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekhiye, aapke dwara diye gaye technician report aur Consumer Protection Act ke sections ko humne note kar liya hai. Company policy ke mutabik, hum aapko 48 ghante ke andar ek senior manager se baat karne ka avsar denge, lekin aapko original invoice, delivery challan aur report ki scanned copy turant upload karni hogi. In documents ki verification ke baad hi hum aapka refund ya replacement process kar sakenge. Kripya yeh sabhi details abhi upload kar dein, tab hum aage ki karwai karenge.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: Aapne specific sections (2(11) aur 84) ka zikr kiya aur technician report ka proof diya, jo aapke daave ko bahut majboot banata hai.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Consumer Protection (E‑commerce) Rules, 2020 ke [unverified reference removed] aur 20 ka bhi ullekh karein, jo seller ko defective goods ke liye free repair/replacement ya refund dene ki zimmedari batata hai. Saath hi, aapke order ki exact purchase date aur delivery date ka zikr karen.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Maine sabhi required documents upload kar diye hain, ab turant refund ya replacement process karne ki maang karta/ti hoon, warna consumer court mein case file kar dunga/dugi.
